standards-1.text: [important] `tests/scripts/test_left_undone_fixture.py`, `session_write_plants` (PY9, R15): the route checks pass for the wrong reason. The file is tampered before the routes run (`lu_file.write_text(original.replace(first, re.sub(r"(?<=: )\d+", ...` at about line 270). The loop then asserts `own("A", f"a check fails a session that wrote left-undone.txt by {name}", bool(hit), ...)`, where `caught()` accepts any failing check whose name matches `left.undone|section|queue line`. The script-output check fails on every route, so a route the detector misses still passes. Fix: run each route on the untampered file and assert that "the session did not write left-undone.txt itself" fails for it.

spec-1.text: [important] (writer's text) `tests/skills/wiki-cycle/check.py:3203-3204`: the write detector misses routes the requirement names. Intent, requirements line 43: "the write detector must catch every route by which the session itself produces `left-undone.txt`". Implemented: the "copy or move into it" pattern lists `cp|mv|install|ln|rsync|Copy-Item|Move-Item|Rename-Item`. It has no `copy`, `move`, `ren` or `xcopy` aliases, and no `>|`. standards-16.text: [important] (writer's text) G2, C2 `tests/skills/wiki-cycle/check.py:3197-3202, 3203-3211, 3207, 3221`: the comment promises "a command that only reads the file ... is not a hit", but reads still match, because the file is anchored by position (last argument) and the verb or alias is matched anywhere before it, not in command position. Probed with `uv run python -B` against `_lu_model_wrote_file` (each returned a hit): `grep -c copy <file>`, `grep move <file>`, `grep ni <file>`, `grep -i sc <file>`, `Select-String -Pattern ac -Path <file>` (aliases `ni`, `sc`, `ac`, `clc` in `_LU_PS_RE`), `grep tee <file>`, `grep -c install <file>`, `tee report.md < <file>`, `[IO.File]::WriteAllText('report.md', [IO.File]::ReadAllText('<file>'))`, `truncate -r <file> other.txt`, `Copy-Item a -Destination <file>.bak`. Round-1 standards-3's own example (`Add-Content ... -Value (Get-Content <file>)`) is fixed and passes; its siblings are not. Affected: a session that only reads the file fails "the session did not write left-undone.txt itself", turning a paid case red for the wrong reason. The fixture's only read control is the `Add-Content` form (`test_left_undone_fixture.py:297`). Fix: match copy verbs, `tee`, `truncate` and PowerShell aliases only as the command word (start, or after `;`, `&`, `|`, `(`), and add `-Destination` an end anchor; add a read control per shape to the fixture. Back to eval-case-writer as a replay.

standards-17.text: [important] (writer's text) G2 `check.py:3209-3213, 3249-3263`: literal write routes the rule claims to catch are missed. Probed, each returned no hit: `cp /tmp/a <file> 2>&1` (the copy pattern needs the file at the end of the command, `:3211`), `open('left-undone.txt', mode='w')` (`:3213` needs a quote straight after the comma), `Set-Content -Path:<file> -Value x`, `shutil.copy('a','left-undone.txt')`, `rni a <file>`, `Export-Csv -Path <file>`, `Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile <file>`. From reading `_lu_ps_writes_file`: `New-Item -Path <dir> -Name left-undone.txt`, an unlisted switch such as `-Confirm:$false` placed before the path, and a quoted `-Value "a|b"` cut at `|` before tokenizing also lose the destination. CHANGELOG.md line 10 and PENDING.md line 28 list `cp, mv, copy ...` as caught; that holds for the bare form only. Fix: allow redirections after the file, accept `mode=`, read `-Path:value`, add the missing aliases and cmdlets, tokenize before splitting on `;|&`; one fixture route per branch. Replay through eval-case-writer. (The Spec axis raises the same gap against the requirement; reported there separately.)
